jobs.summary: Neonatal Nurse Practitioner (NNP) - Peds Neonatology at UNC Children's Hospital. Setting: NICU / neonatology.
jobs.description:
Have you considered a Neonatal Nurse Practitioner career with UNC Health? We are reaching out to share an exciting opportunity with you! This opportunity is eligible for a $10,000 commitment incentive with a three-year commitment. Become part of an inclusive organization with over 40,000 diverse employees, whose mission is to improve the health and well-being of the unique communities we serve.

The individual selected for this position will function as a Neonatal Nurse Practitioner (NNP) delivering critical care medical management in the Newborn Critical Care Center based at the North Carolina Children’s Hospital, the delivery rooms of the North Carolina Women’s Hospital, components of the UNC Hospitals, as well as the brand-new North Carolina Surgical Hospital. The practitioner works in a multi-disciplinary, academic environment and interacts at all professional levels (including students, residents, fellows, faculty and staff) of medical, surgical, nursing, respiratory therapy, and other medical allied health professionals.

UNC Children's Hospital was listed as the America's Best Children's Hospital by U.S. News and World Reports for the 11th year in a row. UNC's Newborn Critical Care Center (NCCC) is a 74-bed level IV intensive care. It is located on the 4thand 6thfloors of North Carolina Children's Hospital and served by 16 board-certified attending neonatologists, 32 nurse practitioners, and more than 150 neonatal specialists. The NCCC underwent an expansion in September 2024, opening 22 single patient rooms, including 2 spacious twin rooms, on the 6thfloor of the Children’s Hospital.

Learn more about this opportunity and apply!

Do you have questions about our opportunities or want assistance finding the opportunity that fits your goals? Reach out to our Recruiter, Josh, at Joshua.Cosby@unchealth.unc.edu. He would be happy to help you take the next step in joining our One Great Team!

Why UNC Health?

UNC Health is a not-for-profit integrated healthcare system owned by the state of North Carolina. With nearly 40,000 employees across the state, our mission is to improve the health and well-being of the unique communities we serve -- from the mountains to the coast! Headquartered in Chapel Hill and affiliated with the University of North Carolina School of Medicine, UNC Health is currently comprised of 14 hospitals, 20 hospital campuses, and more than 900 clinics statewide.

We are committed to supporting teammates from recruitment to retirement. Our UNC Health for Me framework includes ways we welcome, engage, develop, care for, include, and value our teammates. Click here to learn more about this initiative!

Employment at UNC Health is so much more than just a job - we're focused on your health, your wealth, and your career.

The practitioner has responsibility for complete daily medical management of a caseload of critically ill newborn infants including: delivery room resuscitation, initial stabilization, mechanical ventilation, parenteral drug administration, emergency management, acute and continuous medical care of the infant and communication with the infant’s family. Appropriately performs medical procedures consistent with departmental guidelines, privileging, and clinical roles/responsibilities.

Attends education programs based on identified learning needs.

jobs.description:
Pediatric Nurse Practitioner Opportunity in beautiful Western, NC

• UNC Caldwell is the choice for health care in Caldwell County. The Emergency Department sees approximately 30,000 visits a year. Caldwell Physicians and UNC Health Medical Group provide the majority of primary care and select specialty care to our market from thirteen separate medical park locations and 137 bed hospital. Caldwell is seeking a Pediatric NP for a position in a traditional outpatient model with a team of experienced partners.
• Location in the Blue Ridge Mountains – the heart of Northwestern North Carolina with a temperate 4 climate seasons
• Location- The Falls Pediatrics, 4355 Hickory Blvd., Lower Suite, Granite Falls, North Carolina 28630
• A variety of things to do: outdoor recreation, art, music, cycling, water sports, hiking and more
• Proximity to higher education opportunities: Appalachian State University in Boone, NC; Lenoir-Rhyne University in Hickory, NC; Caldwell Community College & Technical Institute in Hudson, NC; and an excellent pre-K thru 12 Public School System that includes an Early College High School
• One hour-and-ten-minute travel time each to: Charlotte Douglas International Airport; the eclectic attractions of Asheville; the arts and history of Winston-Salem; and only 20 minutes to the North Carolina High Country and the mountain seasonal resort community of Blowing Rock.

Practice Highlights:

• Collaborative team of 5 providers in a busy/mature practice!
• Patient Contact hours: 36 hours of patient care; 4 days of clinic / week – Primary Pediatric practice (newborn to 18 yrs of age). Well-child visits, Sick-child visits. Assist with intermittent Falls Peds Urgent Care coverage.
• Located next to a Pediatric Urgent Care, the only one in the region. It is located in an Upper Suite at The Falls Pediatrics, open seven days per week with a dedicated staff.

To be considered, please email your CV to Sheila.Barnes@unchealth.unc.edu

Other Information

● Completion of an accredited graduate-level Advanced Practice Provider (APRN or PA) program.

● Licensed as an Advanced Practice Provider (i.e., Nurse Practitioner, Physician Assistant, Clinical Pharmacist Practitioner, Certified Nurse Midwife, Certified Registered Nurse Anesthetist) in the state of North Carolina.
● Board certification if required by the Department. DEA.
Professional Experience Requirements:
● No prior experience required.

● Demonstrated clinical competency.
● Effective leadership skills. Strong interpersonal skills.
● Ability to work independently and collaboratively.
● Demonstrated written and verbal communication and strong analytical skills.
● Effective interaction to ensure the successful care of patients in the clinical setting.
● Documentation in the medical record to substantiate accurate billing.

Job Description

Description

UNC Health Medical Group Neonatology at Lenoir, in partnership with UNC Health Lenoir, located in Kinston, NC, is currently seeking certified Neonatal Nurse Practitioners to work full time at our Level 1 Nursery. We also have opportunities for Per Diem. You will be part of a highly educated and trained team of physicians (pediatricians and consulting neonatologists) and nurses with the aim of providing excellent care to newborns. This position allows for flexibility and seeks strong experience and leadership qualities. Our daily census is very manageable and allows for day-to-day flexibility for a strong and experienced candidate. The role requires the ability to practice independently, with ample remote support from experienced MDs.

Schedule:

• Days: 7 days on - 7 days off – there is a potential for this model to be adjusted based on candidate experience
• 7:00am-7:00pm – there is overnight call covered by other providers
• Full time and Per Diem openings!

Responsibilities:

• Primary caregiver in Level 1 Nursery to newborn infants
• Assessing & diagnosing newborn infants
• Prescribing medication on your own authority with the agreement of supervising physician
• Educating/supporting parents/guardians in the care of their newborn
• Ordering/performing medical tests and procedures
• Working independently with remote MD support
• Preparing for transfer, if needed, to local Level 2-3 NICUs
• Comfort and experience with procedures such as neonatal intubations and central line placements is highly sought after and preferred

Qualifications:

• Certified Neonatal Nurse Practitioner
• L&D, Nursery or Pediatric NP work experience required
• Work independently with remote supervising physician oversight

Compensation:

• Very Competitive Salary
• Full benefits (Medical + Dental + Vision)
• Retirement Plan
• PTO and CME

Full-Time | Inpatient & Outpatient | Weekend & Holiday Required

The Department of Pediatrics seeks a full-time Advanced Practice Provider (Nurse Practitioner or Physician Assistant) to join the Division of Pediatric Hematology/Oncology. This position provides comprehensive, evidence-based care to children, adolescents, and young adults with malignant and non-malignant hematologic disorders across inpatient and outpatient settings.

The APP will serve as an essential member of a multidisciplinary academic team and will play an active role in clinical care, education, quality improvement, and participation in clinical research and therapeutic trials.

This position will involve primarily weekend coverage with the possibility of outpatient clinic responsibilities for admissions and follow up visits.

Clinical Responsibilities

Inpatient Care

• Conduct daily rounds in collaboration with attending physicians, fellows, residents, pharmacists, and nursing teams
• Manage acute hematologic, oncologic and bone marrow transplant emergencies (e.g., febrile neutropenia, tumor lysis syndrome, sickle cell pain)
• Perform admission evaluations, ongoing assessments, and discharge planning
• Order and interpret laboratory and diagnostic studies
• Participate in weekend and holiday coverage

Outpatient Care

• Perform independent and collaborative visits under physician supervision, as appropriate
• Manage outpatient oncology patients across the care continuum (active treatment, follow-up, survivorship)
• Provide same-day urgent/symptom-based evaluations to reduce ED utilization
• Manage chemotherapy and supportive care regimens
• Monitor treatment response and manage therapy-related complications
• Provide patient and family education regarding diagnosis, treatment plans, and symptom management
• Conduct chemotherapy education and supportive care counseling for patients and families
• Coordinate care across specialties, infusion services, and external providers
• Document and bill patient encounters in compliance with institutional and regulatory standards

Procedures (within scope of practice)

• Lumbar punctures
• Bone marrow aspirates and biopsies
• Ommaya tap
• Intrathecal chemotherapy administration
• Central line management

Clinical Trials & Research Participation

• Provide direct clinical care to patients enrolled in institutional, cooperative group, and industry-sponsored clinical trials
• Ensure protocol adherence in collaboration with principal investigators and research coordinators
• Perform study-related assessments and documentation
• Assist with eligibility screening and informed consent processes (as permitted by scope and institutional policy)
• Monitor for and report adverse events in accordance with regulatory standards
• Participate in multidisciplinary tumor boards and research meetings
• Contribute to quality improvement initiatives and opportunities for scholarly activity, including presentations and publications

Academic Engagement

• Participate in the education of residents, fellows, nurse practitioner students, and physician assistant students
• Attend and contribute to divisional conferences, case reviews, and morbidity and mortality discussions
• Engage in ongoing professional development and academic scholarship

Schedule

• Full-time position
• Combination of inpatient and outpatient responsibilities
• Weekend and holiday coverage required

• Graduate of an accredited Nurse Practitioner or Physician Assistant program
• Current state licensure and national board certification
• DEA registration
• Pediatric clinical experience required
• BLS and PALS certification

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience in pediatric hematology/oncology
• Experience caring for patients enrolled in clinical trials
• Familiarity with research protocols and regulatory requirements
• Experience in academic medical center environment

Core Competencies

• Advanced clinical reasoning in medically complex pediatric populations
• Strong understanding of research integrity and protocol compliance
• Excellent communication and interdisciplinary collaboration skills
• Commitment to family-centered, compassionate care
• Ability to balance clinical productivity with academic engagement

jobs.description:
Your passion belongs at UNC Health. Join more than 56,000 teammates working together to improve the health and well-being of the communities we serve across North Carolina.

Position Summary

The UNC Department of Pediatrics, Division of Pediatric Pulmonology, is seeking a part-time Nurse Practitioner (NP) to join the UNC Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia (BPD) Interdisciplinary Care Program. This is an exciting opportunity to join a growing multidisciplinary program dedicated to improving the care and long-term outcomes of infants and children with BPD and other respiratory complications of prematurity.

The UNC BPD Program provides interdisciplinary care for medically complex infants and children with BPD across the continuum from the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) through childhood. The program brings together specialists from pediatric pulmonology, neonatology, cardiology, nutrition, developmental therapies, respiratory therapy, social work, and other disciplines to provide coordinated, evidence-based care. Through a recently funded program expansion, the team is developing a comprehensive outpatient interdisciplinary BPD program while expanding education, consultation, and outreach to healthcare partners across North Carolina.

The APP will serve as a key clinical member of the BPD team and will work closely with pediatric pulmonologists with expertise in BPD, with opportunities for mentorship and professional development in the care of infants and children with chronic lung disease of prematurity. The position will also support inpatient pulmonary consultation for children with BPD and participate in program development, care coordination, education, quality improvement, and outreach activities.

BPD Program Responsibilities

Specific responsibilities will include:

• Provide outpatient evaluation and longitudinal management of established infants and children with BPD and other respiratory complications of prematurity, in collaboration with pediatric pulmonologists.
• Participate in multidisciplinary BPD clinics, coordinating care with neonatology, cardiology, nutrition, developmental specialists, social work, respiratory therapy, and other disciplines.
• Assist with inpatient pediatric pulmonary consultation and longitudinal care planning for infants and children with BPD, including transition planning from the NICU to outpatient pulmonary care.
• Manage common BPD-related outpatient needs, including supplemental oxygen and respiratory equipment, respiratory medications, symptom management, diagnostic testing, and ongoing assessment of respiratory status.
• Provide education and counseling to patients and families regarding BPD, respiratory therapies, home oxygen and equipment, medications, and anticipatory guidance.
• Participate in multidisciplinary BPD team meetings and contribute to development and implementation of standardized clinical pathways, protocols, and evidence-based care practices.
• Support quality improvement and program evaluation activities, including patient outcome tracking and development of the BPD patient registry.
• Participate in education and outreach activities for healthcare professionals within UNC and at collaborating hospitals and community practices across North Carolina.

About the UNC BPD Program

UNC Children's currently cares for more than 100 new infants with BPD each year and has developed an interdisciplinary inpatient BPD program for infants with moderate-to-severe lung disease. The program is now expanding to establish comprehensive interdisciplinary outpatient care, strengthen transitions from the NICU to home, and increase access to BPD expertise throughout North Carolina.

The BPD Interdisciplinary Care and Outreach Program is supported by a grant from The Duke Endowment and is designed to establish a sustainable model of coordinated BPD care across inpatient, outpatient, and community settings. The program is partnering with hospitals and healthcare professionals across North Carolina to expand access to BPD expertise, develop educational resources and standardized care practices, and improve long-term outcomes for children affected by prematurity.

Preferred Qualifications

• Licensed as an Advanced Practice Provider (Pediatric Nurse Practitioner, Physician Assistant, etc.) in the state of North Carolina
• Prior experience in pediatric pulmonology, neonatology/NICU (including experience as a Neonatal Nurse Practitioner), complex care, pediatric critical care, or the care of medically complex infants and children is preferred but not required.
• Interest in longitudinal care of infants and children with chronic lung disease and medical complexity.
• Strong communication and collaborative skills and an interest in interdisciplinary team-based care.

Interest in clinical program development, quality improvement, patient/family education, and/or community outreach is desirable.

This advanced practice clinician (PA or APN) Surgical Assistant (SA) is an essential member of the pediatric robotic-assisted surgery program at UNC Children’s, and will be instrumental in the growth and success of this program. The SA will act as “bedside assist” for robotic-assisted cases with the Davinci DV5 deployed to the Children’s Operating Room (COR). The SA will have or attain technical certification through Intuitive training program, and maintain proficiency in new and emerging methods, techniques, and tools used in robotic-assisted and minimally-invasive surgery. In cases, the SA will assist with trocar placement; camera management; docking and undocking of actuators; instrument changes; passing of suture, staplers, etc; and closing. The SA will also assist with aspects of perioperative management (e.g. transfers, positioning, padding, pre-check of devices, etc) of the patient for safe and precise procedures. The SA may be recruited to assist in other procedures, especially minimally invasive procedures, depending on need and availability. Most work will be with Pediatric General & Thoracic Surgery and with Pediatric Urology, but as the program expands may include other pediatric surgical specialties (e.g. ENT, cardiac). The SA will maintain robotic certification and personal case logs. This position is housed in the Department of Surgery.

jobs.summary: Advanced Practice Provider (NP/PA) - Radiology - VIR at UNC Children's Hospital. Notable: FNP accepted.
jobs.description:
Become part of an inclusive organization with over 40,000 teammates, whose mission is to improve the health and well-being of the unique communities we serve.

Summary:
A Nurse Practitioner/Physician Assistant functions as part of the interdisciplinary healthcare team in accordance with privileges approved by the credentialing committee to provide high quality, cost effective care to patients within the APPs scope of practice in collaboration with a supervising physician. The APP reflects the mission, vision, and values of the organization, and complies with all relevant policies, procedures, guidelines and other regulatory and accreditation standards.

Nurse Practitioners (FNP) expressing interest must be credentialed to work with both pediatric and adult patients.

Responsibilities:
1. Clinical- Obtains relevant health and medical history, performs thorough physical assessment, reviews and interprets pertinent diagnostic tests/results. Develops appropriate differential diagnoses. Develops and implements treatment plans including prescribing/ordering of appropriate evidence-based pharmacological agents consistent with departmental guidelines and privileging, and schedules appropriate follow-up management. Actively incorporates evidence-based hospital initiatives to improve patient care. Conducts preventive health screening based on age, history and patient needs. Maintains clear comprehensive yet concise records of all aspects of patient care. Maintains essential knowledge of general disease and pathologic processes. Maintains extensive knowledge of their specialty literature including awareness of developing areas. Consistently derives correct diagnoses through synthesis of clinical data and proper selection and interpretation of diagnostic studies. Develops comprehensive differential diagnoses for patients. Revises the plan of care to meet the changing needs of the patient. Prioritizes work and assists staff to provide prompt and efficient client flow. Consistently maintains high productivity according to identified standards. Leads/participates in projects to improve productivity. Appropriately performs medical procedures consistent with departmental guidelines, privileging, and clinical roles/responsibilities.
2. Education- Appropriately and professionally educates clients and/or families regarding medical condition, treatment, and follow-up. Collaborates with clinicians, staff, and students to promote continuity and patient/family centered care. Develops educational materials based on learning needs of clinicians, staff, and students. Provide education/instruction to physicians, housestaff, nursing, ancillaries and/or students. Actively recognizes and participates in identification and achievement of self-learning needs. Attends education programs based on identified learning needs.
3. Leadership- Provides instruction to physicians, housestaff, nursing, ancillaries and/or students including but not limited to precepting, shadowing, lectures, training classes, CE, rounds, morning report, and or staff meetings. Participates in community/network outreach programs. Develops/leads community/network outreach programs. Demonstrates both an understanding of the contexts and system in which healthcare is provided and the ability to apply this knowledge to improve and optimize health care delivery. Leads/participates in systems improvements.
4. Professional- Interacts with patients and families in a respectful, courteous and timely fashion using appropriate communication for the patient and situation. Interacts collaboratively with coworkers, other team members and staff in a respectful, courteous, and timely fashion appropriate to patient care needs and situations. Responds quickly to meet customer needs and resolve problems. Accepts responsibility for outcomes of one?s work. Shares responsibility for overall workload with team members.
5. Quality/Research- Engages in daily continuous quality improvement by identifying and implementing processes for improvement. Consults with management in assessment, problem-solving, decision-making, and evaluating clinical/system issues and models of care. Leads interdisciplinary teams to provide integrated delivery of patient care services. Initiates and revises protocol(s) or guideline(s) to reflect evidence-based changes in care management Works to influence policy-making bodies to improve patient care. Develops new clinical programs or services within the department/unit/clinic to improve patient care.

Other Information

● Licensed as an Advanced Practice Provider (i.e., Nurse Practitioner, Physician Assistant, Clinical Pharmacist Practitioner, Certified Nurse Midwife, Certified Registered Nurse Anesthetist) in the state of North Carolina.
● Board certification if required by the Department. DEA.
Professional Experience Requirements:
● No prior experience required.

● Demonstrated clinical competency.
● Effective leadership skills. Strong interpersonal skills.
● Ability to work independently and collaboratively.
● Demonstrated written and verbal communication and strong analytical skills.
● Effective interaction to ensure the successful care of patients in the clinical setting.
● Documentation in the medical record to substantiate accurate billing.

Your passion belongs at UNC Health. Join more than 56,000 teammates working together to improve the health and well-being of the communities we serve across North Carolina.

UNC Cardiology has a great team of APPs, and we are looking to add to it! Both NPs and PAs are welcome to apply.

This particular job post is to add multiple APPs to our per diem Cardiology APP pool. Currently all Cardiology APP positions (including per diem) work weekday daytime hours only, except for our Critical Care team. We have had APPs in our pool who have worked a wide range of schedules, from an occasional shift once in a while to almost full-time hours regularly – though the norm is much more in the middle. Most candidates hired into this pool are early career APPs and/or want flexibility in their schedule that isn’t possible with full-time positions. We have multiple locations, mostly in and around Chapel Hill – although occasionally assignments outside the Triangle become available for those who can work them. Our per diems may be asked to work in either inpatient our outpatient environments – willingness to work in either environment is preferred but not required.

Summary:
A Nurse Practitioner functions as part of the interdisciplinary healthcare team in accordance with privileges approved by the credentialing committee to provide high quality, cost effective care to patients within the APPs scope of practice in collaboration with a supervising physician. The APP reflects the mission, vision, and values of the organization, and complies with all relevant policies, procedures, guidelines and other regulatory and accreditation standards.

Responsibilities:
1. Clinical- Obtains relevant health and medical history, performs thorough physical assessment, reviews and interprets pertinent diagnostic tests/results. Develops appropriate differential diagnoses. Develops and implements treatment plans including prescribing/ordering of appropriate evidence-based pharmacological agents consistent with departmental guidelines and privileging, and schedules appropriate follow-up management. Actively incorporates evidence-based hospital initiatives to improve patient care. Conducts preventive health screening based on age, history and patient needs. Maintains clear comprehensive yet concise records of all aspects of patient care. Maintains essential knowledge of general disease and pathologic processes. Maintains extensive knowledge of their specialty literature including awareness of developing areas. Consistently derives correct diagnoses through synthesis of clinical data and proper selection and interpretation of diagnostic studies. Develops comprehensive differential diagnoses for patients. Revises the plan of care to meet the changing needs of the patient. Prioritizes work and assists staff to provide prompt and efficient client flow. Consistently maintains high productivity according to identified standards. Leads/participates in projects to improve productivity. Appropriately performs medical procedures consistent with departmental guidelines, privileging, and clinical roles/responsibilities.
2. Education- Appropriately and professionally educates clients and/or families regarding medical condition, treatment, and follow-up. Collaborates with clinicians, staff, and students to promote continuity and patient/family centered care. Develops educational materials based on learning needs of clinicians, staff, and students. Provide education/instruction to physicians, housestaff, nursing, ancillaries and/or students. Actively recognizes and participates in identification and achievement of self-learning needs. Attends education programs based on identified learning needs.
3. Leadership- Provides instruction to physicians, housestaff, nursing, ancillaries and/or students including but not limited to precepting, shadowing, lectures, training classes, CE, rounds, morning report, and or staff meetings. Participates in community/network outreach programs. Develops/leads community/network outreach programs. Demonstrates both an understanding of the contexts and system in which healthcare is provided and the ability to apply this knowledge to improve and optimize health care delivery. Leads/participates in systems improvements.
4. Professional- Interacts with patients and families in a respectful, courteous and timely fashion using appropriate communication for the patient and situation. Interacts collaboratively with coworkers, other team members and staff in a respectful, courteous, and timely fashion appropriate to patient care needs and situations. Responds quickly to meet customer needs and resolve problems. Accepts responsibility for outcomes of one?s work. Shares responsibility for overall workload with team members.
5. Quality/Research- Engages in daily continuous quality improvement by identifying and implementing processes for improvement. Consults with management in assessment, problem-solving, decision-making, and evaluating clinical/system issues and models of care. Leads interdisciplinary teams to provide integrated delivery of patient care services. Initiates and revises protocol(s) or guideline(s) to reflect evidence-based changes in care management Works to influence policy-making bodies to improve patient care. Develops new clinical programs or services within the department/unit/clinic to improve patient care.

● Board certification if required by the Department. DEA.
Professional Experience Requirements:
● No prior experience required.

jobs.title: Psychiatric Advanced Practice Provider (PMHNP or PA) - Psychiatric Emergency Services
jobs.summary: Psychiatric Advanced Practice Provider (PMHNP or PA) - Psychiatric Emergency Services at UNC Children's Hospital. Notable: nights.
jobs.description:
Your passion belongs at UNC Health. Join more than 56,000 teammates working together to improve the health and well-being of the communities we serve across North Carolina.

Description:

The Department of Emergency Medicine at the University of North Carolina is seeking a Psychiatric Advanced Practice Provider (PMHNP or Physician Assistant with relevant psychiatric training) to join the Emergency Department’s Psychiatric Emergency Service (PES). This provider is responsible for the screening, ongoing evaluation, and treatment of patients presenting with mental health and/or substance use–related concerns in the Emergency Department.

The APP will augment the primary emergency medicine team by providing psychiatric assessment, diagnosis, and treatment, including but not limited to:

• Performing comprehensive psychiatric evaluations and establishing diagnoses
• Responding to behavioral emergencies
• Providing brief supportive therapy
• Prescribing and ordering evidence-based psychopharmacologic treatments
• Making recommendations regarding involuntary commitment when appropriate
• Collaborating with a multidisciplinary crisis team on resources and disposition planning
• Obtain relevant medical and psychiatric history, perform focused physical assessments, and review and interpret pertinent diagnostic tests and results.
• Timely and thorough documentation of psychiatric consult notes, including assessment and medical decision-making, treatment recommendations (including level of care), patient history, diagnoses, and mental status examinations.
• Prior emergency department and/or psychiatric crisis experience
• North Carolina First Commitment Certification Strong written and verbal communication skills, excellent organization, and the ability to function effectively in a fast-paced emergency department environment are essential.

Preferred Qualifications

• Prior emergency department and/or psychiatric crisis experience
• North Carolina First Commitment Certification Additional Benefits
• Eligible for evening and weekend shift differentials
• Eligible for continuing medical education (CME) reimbursement through the Department of Emergency Medicine.

Schedule:

• Nights

jobs.description:

Summary:
The Advanced Practice Provider (PA/NP) Manager is an APP with demonstrated leadership skills and clinical excellence. This individual provides operational and supervisory support for APPs in their area(s) and works collaboratively with the APP Center, department leadership and other key stakeholders to establish and maintain an optimized APP strategy and workforce plan. The APP Manager is responsible for direct oversight of APP Supervisors (~15 direct reports) and some practicing APPs (total roll-up of approx. 30-60 APPs). This position requires both administrative (20%) and clinical (80%) time. Actual split may vary depending on the number and work location of direct reports.

Responsibilities:
1. Strategy: Designs and implements an APP strategy that improves clinical care through optimizing the utilization of APPs in respective area based on internal and external benchmarks, survey data and data management tools.
2. Clinical Practice and Performance Improvement: Meets regularly with APP Center and department leadership to monitor APP performance metrics including productivity, utilization and access, and quality to identify opportunities for improvement. Develops and oversees implementation and enforcement of policies and procedures related to APP clinical practice and works with APP Supervisors and/or leadership to resolve concerns. Ensures adherence to APP regulatory processes (credentialing/privileging, internal standards, clinical protocols, compliance training, Collaborative Practice Agreement). Communicates and meets regularly with both APP Supervisors and APP clinical staff.
3. Human Resources: Implements leading practices in recruitment, onboarding, orienting, retaining, and mentoring of APP workforce. Ensures appropriately trained APPs are hired for scope of practice, patient population and roles/responsibilities. Completes personnel functions and disciplinary actions using hospital and departmental guidelines. Approves service schedules, PTO, leave requests, and payroll administration.

Educates, monitors, and approves APP effort in TimeTrex. Ensure education is provided regarding optimal APP billing and documentation practices.
5. Professional Development: Assess learning needs of APP staff and students. Mentors and provides professional development opportunities for APP providers and students in areas of leadership, clinical excellence, patient centered care, education, research, quality improvement and organizational involvement.

jobs.summary: NNP, PNP-AC or PA - NICU Portland, ME at Barbara Bush Children's Hospital. Setting: NICU / neonatology. Notable: sign-on bonus, new grad friendly, nights, CPNP-AC required, relocation assistance.
jobs.description:
Maine Medical Center Barbara Bush Children’s Hospital in Portland, Maine - Maine’s only full-service Level IV NICU children’s hospital, is recruiting for an experienced Advanced Practice Provider (APP); a Neonatal Nurse Practitioner, Acute Care Certified Pediatric Nurse Practitioner, or a Physician Associate/Assistant. This is a combined day and night position and new grads with a strong neonatal background are encouraged to apply.

The APP will provide detailed and comprehensive assessment and treatment of neonatal patients within the framework of safe patient and family centered care. The APP will be responsible for attending high-risk deliveries, as well as functioning as the lead on neonatal transports. The scope of practice encompasses the development and recording of a plan for care in collaboration with family, multidisciplinary team members, and community resources for both chronic and episodic illnesses.

Desired Qualifications & Experience:

·Excellence in interpersonal and communication skills to interact effectively with all MHMMC departments, families, and members of the multidisciplinary health care team.

·Advanced knowledge of nursing theory and practice, and/or additional specialized medical training, to provide expanded practice at a level generally acquired through completion of concentrated study and clinical internship leading to a Master's Degree.

·Analytical abilities necessary to obtain medical histories, conduct physical examinations, prepare complex treatment plans, and provide care for assigned patients with minimal guidance and direction.

What We Offer:

Our position offers variable scheduling. Off shift requirements (nights/weekends/holidays) are shared equally within the group. In addition, we offer a sign on bonus; relocation assistance, if qualified; CME reimbursement, and other great benefits.

Education:

·Completion of accredited NNP, PNP Acute Care Certification or PA.

Licensure:

jobs.summary: Nurse Practitioner or Physician Assistant, Complex Care Svs. (24 hrs) at Boston Children's Hospital. Setting: mixed settings. Notable: sign-on bonus, new grad friendly, nights, FNP accepted.
jobs.description:
Nurse Practitioner or Physician Assistant - Complex Care Services

Department Summary
Nurse Practitioner (NP) or Physician Assistant (PA) to function in the inpatient Complex Care Service (CCS) at Boston Children’s Hospital. CCS is a long-standing and nationally-regarded inpatient service within the Division of General Pediatrics that serves hospitalized children with medical complexity, who have complex chronic conditions and functional limitations. Common reasons for admission to CCS include infections (aspiration pneumonia, pyelonephritis), chronic condition exacerbations (epilepsy, digestive dysmotility), and post-operative recovery following surgery (baclofen pump placement, gastrostomy, spinal fusion, etc.). This role will provide patient evaluation, assessment, and facilitate care for the patients on the CCS service and will implement interventions tailored to improve systems for patient care and enhance patient safety for this population. The CCS NP/PA will work collaboratively with supervising physicians, pediatric trainees (residents and fellows), and the entire nursing team to promote optimal clinical care. The setting is fast-paced and collaborative with many opportunities for learning. Requirements include completion of a master’s degree program in Nursing or Physician Assistant Studies. Clinical experience with children with medical complexity is preferred.

Key Responsibilities
• Evaluate, assess, and facilitate care for medical and surgical patients with medical complexity admitted to the Complex Care Service.
• Help implement interventions to improve care systems and enhance patient safety.
• Collaborate with supervising physicians and the nursing/medical team to promote optimal care.
• Act as a clinical resource and facilitate staff educational opportunities.
• Participate in learning, quality improvement, and/or research initiatives.
• 24-hours/week with 50% day/night rotation and every 3rd weekend; 12-hour shifts.

Minimal Qualifications
Education
• Master of Science in Nursing or Master of Science in Physician Assistant Studies.

Experience
• 1+ year of pediatric NP/PA experience preferred.
• Experience with children with medical complexity preferred.
• New graduate NP or PA may be considered with 2+ years of recent pediatric inpatient RN experience or strong inpatient pediatric clinical rotations.

Licensure/Certifications
• Current MA NP or PA license with PNP or FNP certification

This role offers a sign-on bonus of $3,000 . (For those who have not worked at BCH in the past 2 years).

jobs.title: Nurse Practitioner or Physician Assistant, CICU day/night
jobs.summary: Nurse Practitioner or Physician Assistant, CICU day/night at Boston Children's Hospital. Setting: PICU / pediatric critical care. Notable: sign-on bonus, nights.
jobs.description:
Position Summary

We are expanding our Advanced Practice Provider team in a state of the art 44 bed Cardiac Intensive Care Unit in a new Heart Center here at Boston Children’s Hospital. We are looking for diverse and motivated individuals to join our team here in Boston. When you join our team you will work with a supportive group of Advanced Practice Providers, Attending Physicians and Fellows. You will be responsible for taking care of Pre and Post-operative highly acute cardiac patients, along with children who have cardiac medical needs in the intensive care unit. We have an extensive Orientation Program to prepare you for taking care of these critically ill patients and to thrive here at Boston Children’s. Come join a supportive, multidisciplinary and collaborative team that puts the patient and families first through exceptional care and the latest Pediatric Cardiac Research.

Key Responsibilities:

• Providing care to infants, children, and adults with congenital and acquired heart disease.
• Caring for patients with both acute and chronic cardiac disease.
• Collaborating with the CICU Attending physician, to conduct patient assessment, medical history, physical exams, and diagnose health and developmental problems.
• Participating in CICU medical rounds, including presentation of clinical information, plan development and continued management and modification of the plan for patients throughout the shift.
• Pre and Post-Op care of critically ill cardiac patients that involves management of ventilators, inotropic support, ECMO, CVVH, emergency situations and sedation titration.
• Procedures such as Intubation and Central lines, will be taught in both Simulation and during real-time, hands-on events.
• Extensive Orientation Program with a designated preceptor, simulation and didactic classes along with hands-on experience. Access to in-person and Zoom lectures by Heart Center experts as well as electronic recordings on OpenPediatrics.
• Participation in ongoing research and committees in the CICU.
• Offer consultation and education to all staff, patients and families.
• Schedule: 40 hours per week, up to 50% rotation to nights, every 3rd weekend and some holidays, including major.

Minimum Qualifications

Education:

• A graduate degree from an accredited Nurse Practitioner or Physician Assistant program.

Experience:

• A minimum of 2 years of critical care RN, NP or PA experience.
• Possess a solid medical knowledge base for cardiopulmonary critical care medicine with an interest in congenital cardiac anomalies.
• Possess critical thinking skills and adaptability on a busy cardiac intensive care unit.
• Communication skills to work collaboratively with medical and surgical colleagues, staff and trainees.

Licensure/ Certifications:

• A current license from the Commonwealth of Massachusetts to practice as a Nurse Practitioner or Physician Assistant.

This role offers a competitive sign-on bonus ranging from: $5,000 to $20,000, based on your experience. (For those who have not worked at BCH in the past 2 years).

jobs.summary: APP Neonatal ICU NICU at Johns Hopkins Children's Center. Setting: NICU / neonatology. Notable: sign-on bonus, new grad friendly, fellowship, nights.
jobs.description:
The Neonatal Nurse Practitioner or Neonatal Physician Assistant works collaboratively within a multidisciplinary health team and is responsible for providing comprehensive and age-appropriate care to both well and/or ill patients. The NNP or PA educates patients' families and/or intervenes in acute or chronic illnesses. The NNP or PA practices within their scope as defined by their education, specialty certification and the guidelines of the unit, department and institution. The NNP or PA is granted affiliate staff privileges by the Johns Hopkins Hospital Medical Board; these privileges reviewed during re-credentialing.

Shift: Fulltime

Schedule: Rotating, Days and Nights, Weekends and Holidays

**$20,000 sign on bonus for expereinced NICU APP **

Responsibilities:

• Conduct thorough assessments of neonatal patients.
• Collaborate with physicians, nurses, and other healthcare professionals to develop and implement individualized care plans.
• Monitor and manage the ongoing care of patients, adjusting treatment plans as needed.
• Educate and support patients and their families in understanding and managing complex medical conditions.
• Serve as a resource and mentor to other healthcare team members.
• Participate in case conferences and collaborate with specialists to ensure coordinated and comprehensive care.

Qualifications:

• Master's or Doctorate degree in nursing from an accredited NNP program, or Masters in Physician Assistant Studies from an accredited PA program
• Registered Nurse (RN) license and Nurse Practitioner (NP) certification, or PA
• Maryland or Compact RN and CRNP, or MD PA
• Current BLS CPR certification
• Minimum 3 years of acute care RN NICU experience required; Level III or IV NICU experience preferred. PA: Level III or IV NICU experience or completion of a Neonatal Residency or Fellowship.

Salary Range: Minimum 60.93/hour - Maximum 94.45/hour. Compensation will be commensurate with equity and experience for roles of similar scope and responsibility. In cases where the range is displayed as a $0 amount, salary discussions will occur during candidate screening calls, before any subsequent compensation discussion is held between the candidate and any hiring authority.

The Hospital reserves the right to modify employee schedules as needed.

We are committed to creating a welcoming and inclusive environment, where we embrace and celebrate our differences, where all employees feel valued, contribute to our mission of serving the community, and engage in equitable healthcare delivery and workforce practices.

Johns Hopkins Health System and its affiliates are drug-free workplace employers.

jobs.title: NP/PA Supervisor Neonatology
jobs.summary: NP/PA Supervisor Neonatology at K. Hovnanian Children's Hospital. Setting: NICU / neonatology.
jobs.description:
The Neonatal Supervisor Nurse Practitioner or Physician Assistant is responsible to develop and assist administratively and support clinical care on the Clinic and also function as a resource educator to the unit. This includes developing and overseeing clinical care protocols as well as Quality Improvement and Performance Improvement oversight, to ensure continual quality care. This is in addition to delivery of normal daily clinical patient care.

This role is responsible for the comprehensive care of neonates and infants. Care is delivered at Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) and Special Care Nurseries

Core Clinical Duties & Privileges:

• Attend 'high-risk' deliveries at the request of the obstetrician or perinatologist to provide immediate neonatal assessment and resuscitation.
• Perform and manage neonatal consults in the well-baby nursery, pediatric floor, and Pediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU).
• Provide clinical management for infants admitted to the NICU and SCN, including writing admission, procedure and transport notes, managing ventilation, and coordinating care with referring and specialty physicians.
• Attend and communicate with the transport team while on neonatal transports.
• Accompany critically ill infants to the operating room at the request of the pediatric surgeon or anesthesiologist.
• Be available for telephone consults with community pediatricians regarding neonatal concerns.

Academic & Teaching Responsibilities:

• Provide daily teaching rounds with pediatric residents, medical students and other advanced practice providers.
• Formally supervise, review, and co-sign the clinical procedures performed by residents or APP trainees
• Provide formal teaching lectures for residents and medical students as part of the academic curriculum.
• Become and maintain status as a Neonatal Resuscitation Program (NRP) instructor, responsible for teaching NRP courses and running mega-codes for residents, nurses, and other physicians.
• Actively participate in scholarly activities (e.g., research, publications) in support of the Division of Neonatology.
• Attends required educational division conferences

Operational & Scheduling Requirements:

• Provide and ensure 24/7 in-house on-call service for all required locations.
• Provide back-up coverage to other on-service providers and, when required, to the NICU at affiliated medical centers (e.g., JSUMC).
• Attend weekly discharge planning meetings to coordinate and expedite patient discharge plans with case management.

Administrative Responsibilities

• Assists in the selection and evaluation of Nurse Practitioners and Physician Assistants in the Division.
• Oversees the training of all new Nurse Practitioners and Physician Assistants on clinical protocols and procedures.
• Defines job expectations and monitors productivity, including appropriate billing/ coding.
• Responsible for approving and if necessary, assisting with scheduling and assignment of Nurse Practitioners/Physician Assistants to maintain appropriate staffing and coverage.
• Develops and implements process improvement initiatives and procedures for the Nurse Practitioner/Physician Assistants.

jobs.summary: Pediatric Electrophysiologist Nurse Practitioner (NP) or Physician Assistant (PA) at Inova L.J. Murphy Children's Hospital. Notable: relocation assistance.
jobs.description:
The Inova Children’s Heart Center at Inova L.J. Murphy Children’s Hospital is seeking a board-certified Advanced Practice Provider to join our Pediatric Electrophysiology team apart of our nationally recognized and growing pediatric cardiology program in Northern Virginia. This is an exceptional opportunity to become part of a comprehensive congenital heart program that provides advanced, multidisciplinary care to infants, children, adolescents, and adults with congenital heart disease throughout the Greater Washington region.

The Heart Center at Inova L.J. Murphy Children’s Hospital has provided exceptional pediatric cardiac care to Northern Virginia and the Greater Washington region for more than 30 years. The program performs approximately 550 cardiac procedures annually, including surgical repair of the most complex congenital heart defects, such as hypoplastic left heart syndrome.

The Heart Center offers a seamless continuum of care from infancy through adulthood, including a dedicated Adult Congenital Heart Disease Program. The comprehensive team provides expertise across the full spectrum of congenital and pediatric heart care, including congenital cardiac surgery, outpatient and fetal cardiology, noninvasive imaging, adult congenital cardiology, diagnostic and interventional catheterization, electrophysiology, and advanced heart failure therapies.

The Electrophysiology (EP) Program is the largest pediatric and adult congenital heart disease (ACHD) electrophysiology program in Northern Virginia, providing care for more than 2,500 patients. The EP team follows nearly 400 children with pacemakers and implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs), as well as approximately 250 patients enrolled in our dedicated channelopathy program.

The program performs 180–200 procedures annually, including electrophysiology studies, catheter ablations, and device implantations. We utilize the latest advances in cardiac rhythm management, including conduction system pacing, leadless pacemakers, and subcutaneous ICD (S-ICD) systems.

All EP procedures are conducted in a state-of-the-art biplane electrophysiology laboratory equipped with both CARTO™ and EnSite™ three-dimensional mapping systems. These procedures are supported by a highly skilled and collaborative pediatric EP team dedicated to delivering exceptional patient care.

A dedicated advanced practice provider specializing in pediatric electrophysiology oversees remote device monitoring and assists with Holter monitor interpretation. The program is further strengthened by three dedicated pediatric cardiovascular genetic counselors who support our comprehensive channelopathy clinic.

Our cardiogenetics clinic is the largest of its kind in Northern Virginia and provides evaluation and management for children with inherited arrhythmia and cardiomyopathy syndromes, including long QT syndrome, Brugada syndrome, catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (CPVT), hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), and arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC).

Through a close partnership with the adult cardiac services at Inova Schar Heart and Vascular, the program offers seamless referral pathways for cascade genetic testing, family screening, and comprehensive evaluation of inherited cardiac conditions, ensuring coordinated care across the lifespan.

Inova is consistently ranked a national healthcare leader in safety, quality and patient experience. We are also proud to be consistently recognized as a top employer in both the D.C. metro area and the nation.

• CME Support: Up to $3,500 a year for CME support and up to 5 days of CME
• Tuition and Student Loan Assistance: offering up to $5,250 per year in education assistance and up to $10,000 for student loans.
• Work/Life Balance: offering paid time off and paid parental leave

Seeking Breakthrough Makers

Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP) offers countless ways to change lives. Our diverse community of more than 20,000 Breakthrough Makers will inspire you to pursue passions, develop expertise, and drive innovation.

At CHOP, your experience is valued; your voice is heard; and your contributions make a difference for patients and families. Join us as we build on our promise to advance pediatric care—and your career.

CHOP does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, sex, national origin, religion, or any other legally protected categories in any employment, training, or vendor decisions or programs. CHOP recognizes the critical importance of a workforce rich in varied backgrounds and experiences and engages in ongoing efforts to achieve that through equally varied and non-discriminatory means.

A Brief Overview
CHOP is hiring for a full-time Nurse Practitioner to work at our South Philadelphia office. The schedule includes 24 clinical hours and 4 administrative hours. The Nurse Practitioner practices within their Delineation of Practice and under the guidelines of the Division of Ambulatory Care. In collaboration with the attending physician, the Nurse Practitioner provides health care management and support to well and sick children enrolled in the ambulatory care network. The Nurse Practitioner provides assessment and diagnosis, interventions, evaluation and follow-up. The Nurse Practitioner participates in professional leadership activities including quality improvement, education and consultation to the nursing staff. Participation in scholarly activities is a part of the role.

What you will do

• For specific clinical job responsibilities, please refer to Delineation of Practice Document and Clinical Responsibilities checklist.
• Assessment and diagnosis including obtaining a complete health history, performing a physical exam, order and interpreting screening and laboratory tests and diagnostic procedures, making a diagnosis and formulating a family centered plan of care.
• Interventions including treating health concerns, providing patient/family education, providing follow up care, consultation with other health care professionals and making referrals. Perform advanced procedures that are listed in Scope of Practice document and approved as a part of the credentialing process.
• Evaluate and monitor the effective of prescribed treatment plan. Using the most current evidence modify the plan of care based on the effectiveness of treatment and the patient /family response to the plan.
• Participate in scholarly activities including research, publications and education.
• Participate in own professional development by maintaining required competencies, identifying learning needs and seeking appropriate educational offerings. Act as preceptor and mentor to support the development of nurses, nurse practitioners, students and other health care providers.
• Demonstrate commitment to patient safety by speaking up about safety issues and changing practices to enhance safety. Share errors through system reporting mechanisms, and demonstrates shared accountability for safe practices.

Education Qualifications

• Master's Degree Nursing - Required

Skills and Abilities

• Ability to work in an inter-professional team setting with multiple responsibilities. (Required proficiency)
• Ability to use computer and electronic medical record effectively. (Required proficiency)
• Please refer to Scope of Practice document and Clinical Responsibilities checklist for specific requirements. (Required proficiency)
• Computer Competency

• Basic use of Microsoft Office (Word processing, spreadsheets, presentations and Skype). (Required proficiency)

In this role, as a member of the CHOP Fetal APP team, you will care for patients who are pregnant with high-risk fetuses. You will provide prenatal and postnatal care, coordinate multidisciplinary team care, and assist with fetal procedures both in the outpatient clinic and in the operating room. Scrub experience is helpful but not necessary. Previous experience as a Women's Health Nurse Practitioner or Certified Nurse Midwife strongly preferred. Proficiency with fetal heart rate interpretations required in addition to other basic obstetric assessment skills.

The Richard D. Wood Jr. Center for Fetal Diagnosis and Treatment at Children's Hospital of Philadelphia is an internationally recognized leader in fetal diagnosis, fetal surgery and fetal care. We offer highly specialized care to mothers carrying fetuses with known birth defects that require fetal surgery and treatment before or after birth.

Here at our Center, you’ll find comprehensive, family-centered care in one location, from advanced diagnostic testing, prenatal management and fetal surgery to a special delivery unit, counseling and support services, and expert postnatal care. Our Garbose Family Special Delivery Unit was the world’s first birthing unit dedicated to healthy mothers of babies with known birth defects. Since 1995, we’ve cared for more than 28,658 expectant parents from around the world and performed more than 2,104 fetal surgeries, an unparalleled level of experience caring for the tiniest patients before, during, and after delivery that helps us achieve the best outcomes possible.

As part of one of the top-ranked and largest children’s hospitals in the U.S., we have a high volume of patients and treat the full range of fetal anomalies. We’re one of the few fetal centers in the world to offer open fetal surgery for life-threatening conditions, as well as a variety of other fetal interventions such as minimally invasive fetoscopic surgery and ex utero intrapartum therapy. Our team is made up of pioneers in fetal medicine who constantly work to refine and advance the techniques used to treat birth defects.

Join our team and help provide high-quality, compassionate care to critically ill pediatric patients in a dynamic and supportive environment.

Children's Hospital of Philadelphia is hiring APPs to join the Pediatric Critical Care team. • Waterfront living, boating, and outdoor lifestyle

• Support newborns through monitoring and treatment during the transition period after birth

• Perform procedures within scope (e.g., endotracheal intubation, airway management, lumbar puncture, IV access, umbilical line placement, LMA use, thoracentesis)

• Deliver family-centered care, education, and communication throughout the patient journey
• Participate in quality improvement, program development, and development of clinical best practices

• Round daily on patients; examine, evaluate, assess, diagnose, and develop care plans
• Monitor clinical status and initiate interventions as needed
• Order and interpret diagnostic and laboratory studies
• Perform neonatal procedures within scope

• Document care in compliance with clinical standards and protocols
• Contribute to team-based care and program growth initiatives

• Board Certified Neonatal Nurse Practitioner (NNP)
• 1-2 years NNP experience strongly preferred
• Active or eligible RN/APRN licensure
• BLS and NRP required
• Strong communication, clinical judgment, and team collaboration skills
• Experience working with newborns preferred
• While on call, the NNP must be able to physically arrive to the hospital within 20 min

• Competitive compensation
• Full benefits package, CME, and retirement
• Relocation assistance (if applicable)
• Opportunity to build and shape a growing program
• Support from Duke Health

At Duke Health, the FNP role extends beyond clinical care—you will contribute to patient care excellence, education, and program growth, working in an environment that values innovation and continuous improvement.

If you are looking for meaningful clinical work, lifestyle balance, and the ability to influence a growing program, we’d love to connect.

• Lift up to 50 lbs from floor to waist.

Functions independently to perform age-appropriate, disease-specific history and physical examination of complex acute, critical, and chronic advanced heart failure patients.

Rounds daily with interdisciplinary team

Manages care and treatment plan as the front-line provider for patients

Orders and interprets diagnostic and therapeutic tests, including laboratory and radiologic

Monitors the effectiveness of interventions

If it’s possible, you will find it at Atrium Health—the leading community-focused academic healthcare system serving North Carolina and South Carolina. We invite APPs to discover all that we can do when we bring healing hearts, inquisitive minds and progressive visionaries together in our Levine Children’s Hospital team in Charlotte.

The Division of Pediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology, and Nutrition at Atrium Health Levine Children's is seeking an advanced practice practitioner to join our growing outpatient pediatric GI practice. You will work with a talented and collegial group of 14 physicians and 5 advanced practice providers, 5 registered dietitians, 2 dedicated pediatric psychologists, 2 licensed clinical social workers, and an outstanding nursing team and support staff. The practice is based at the Levine Children's Specialty Center on the campus of Atrium Health Levine Children's Hospital, with multiple satellite offices throughout the greater Charlotte region. Our division provides comprehensive services for all children's digestive conditions and has been ranked in the US News & World Report top 25 programs in the country for the last 3 years.

LCH has repeatedly been ranked among the Best Children's Hospitals in the nation by U.S. News & World Report, most recently in seven pediatric specialties for 2024-2025, including Urology, Cardiology and Heart Surgery, Gastroenterology and GI Surgery, Nephrology, Cancer, Orthopedics, and Pulmonology and Lung Surgery. The growing academic department brings exciting opportunities for innovative patient care, team-based care models, teaching, and research.

Position:

This APP position will be a hybrid role to include both inpatient and outpatient coverage, offering a varied patient population. When outpatient, the APP will have their own clinic template with a major focus on long-term management of our large population of enterally tube fed patients (i.e gastrostomy tube, gastrojejunostomy tube), and patients with general gastroenterology conditions including gastroesophageal reflux disease, constipation, abdominal pain, failure to thrive, and milk protein intolerance. Our outpatient APPs also work collaboratively with our inpatient APPs to ensure excellent hospital follow-up for patients needing our services. While inpatient, the APP will see hospitalized patients in collaboration with the gastroenterology attending physicians. The inpatient GI service is primarily a consultation service offering recommendations to the primary team (general pediatrics, PICU, Cardiology, NICU or hematology/oncology), but at times it has primary patients. The candidate will have excellent mentorship from current experienced GI APP's and supportive supervising physicians.

This position has no nighttime call or weekend responsibilities. There are also opportunities for involvement in clinical research and quality improvement projects.

Atrium Health Levine Children's Hospital is seeking an APP to join our growing Pediatric Preventive Cardiology program, part of Advocate Health.

This is a primarily clinical outpatient role focused on the assessment and longitudinal management of children and adolescents with cardiovascular risk factors and conditions that predispose to early cardiovascular disease, with opportunities to participate in research and program development. The successful candidate will deliver care across both in-person and virtual clinics, supporting patients and families throughout North Carolina, South Carolina, and Georgia.

About the Program

Our Pediatric Preventive Cardiology program—based at Levine Children's Hospital and supported by the resources of Advocate Health, one of the nation's largest integrated health systems—provides specialized, evidence-based care aimed at identifying and modifying cardiovascular risk early in life.

The patient population includes children and adolescents with:

· Hypertension and elevated blood pressure

· Familial hypercholesterolemia (heterozygous and homozygous), including cascade-screened family members

· Hypertriglyceridemia and rare genetic dyslipidemias

· Elevated cardiovascular risk secondary to high-risk conditions, including childhood cancer survivors, chronic kidney disease, and inflammatory/autoimmune disorders

The program operates through a hybrid model of in-person clinics and telehealth, expanding access to specialized preventive care across a three-state region.

Key Responsibilities

This is a predominantly clinical position. The majority of the role is dedicated to direct patient care, with protected opportunities for research and program development available to candidates with those interests.

Clinical Care (primary focus)

· Provide comprehensive outpatient evaluation and longitudinal management for the patient populations described above, in collaboration with attending pediatric cardiologists.

· Conduct new-patient evaluations, follow-up visits, lipid and blood pressure management, lifestyle counseling, and pharmacologic management as appropriate.

· Order and interpret relevant diagnostic studies (e.g., lipid panels, ambulatory blood pressure monitoring, echocardiography, and other cardiovascular testing) in coordination with the care team.

· Deliver care through both in-person clinics and virtual/telehealth visits to patients located across North Carolina, South Carolina, and Georgia.

· Provide patient- and family-centered education, including on diet, physical activity, medication adherence, and condition-specific risk reduction.

· Coordinate care with referring providers, primary care, and subspecialists (oncology, nephrology, rheumatology, genetics), as well as community resources.

Research (opportunity)

· Participate in clinical and quality-improvement research within the program, with opportunities to contribute to study design, data collection, and dissemination.

· Support outcomes tracking across the patient population.

Program Development (opportunity)

· Contribute to the development and refinement of clinical pathways and protocols, with a specific focus on the outpatient management of pediatric hypertension.

· Help build and standardize workflows, documentation tools, and care models that scale across in-person and virtual settings and across multiple states.

Qualifications

· Master's or Doctoral degree from an accredited Nurse Practitioner or Physician Assistant program.

· Current certification as a Physician Assistant ( PA-C) or Pediatric Nurse Practitioner (PNP-PC or PNP-AC) or Family Nurse Practitioner (FNP) with relevant pediatric experience.

· Active, unrestricted PA/NP licensure with eligibility to obtain and maintain authorization to practice in North Carolina, South Carolina, and Georgia (multi-state licensure is required to support cross-state telehealth and in-person care).

· DEA registration or eligibility.

Ideal Candidate

· Clinical experience in pediatric cardiology, preventive cardiology, lipidology, or management of pediatric hypertension.

· Experience with telehealth delivery and comfort managing patients across a hybrid in-person/virtual model.

· Familiarity with chronic disease management in high-risk pediatric populations (e.g., cancer survivorship, chronic kidney disease, inflammatory disorders).

· Interest or prior experience in clinical research, quality improvement, or program development.

Practice Setting

This position combines in-person clinic sessions with virtual care, allowing flexible delivery of specialized preventive cardiology services to patients across a three-state catchment area. The role is well suited to a clinician who values direct patient care and the chance to help shape a developing program within an academic children's hospital environment.

Our Commitment to You:

Assist with the coordination of care, ensuring seamless communication among multidisciplinary providers.

Participate in the delivery of specialty care across various settings, including inpatient, outpatient, dialysis, and follow-up care.

Opportunities for future training and involvement in specialized procedures such as dialysis, infusion therapies, renal ultrasound, and percutaneous renal biopsies.

Use medical decision-making skills to determine the appropriate patient care plan.

Collaborate with the medical team when needed for effective team-based care.

Order and interpret laboratory studies and diagnostic procedures. Explain the necessity, preparation, nature, and anticipated effects of scheduled diagnostic and therapeutic procedures to the patient.

Perform procedural skills per department or practice guidelines.

Potential for and encouraged to precept students and/or medical learners.

Uphold AHWFB missions, values, and cultural commitment.

If it’s possible, you will find it at Atrium Health — the leading community-focused academic healthcare system serving North Carolina, South Carolina, and Georgia. We invite Advanced Practice Providers (APPs) to discover all that we can do when we bring healing hearts, inquisitive minds, and visionaries together on our Behavioral Health team at Atrium Health in Charlotte, North Carolina.

Atrium Health is seeking an experienced, full-time Advanced Practice Provider specializing in Behavioral Health to provide comprehensive psychiatric and behavioral health services to patients requiring acute psychiatric evaluation, consultation, and treatment.

This position is open to board-certified Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioners (PMHNP-BC) and Physician Assistants (PA) who are trained and proficient in the delivery of psychiatric services. The provider will support behavioral health consultation services for patients presenting to the emergency department and inpatient care settings, helping ensure timely psychiatric evaluations, appropriate treatment interventions, and effective coordination of care.

Working collaboratively with multidisciplinary healthcare teams, the APP will play a key role in improving access to behavioral health services, facilitating timely patient dispositions, and supporting continuity of care during evening, overnight, weekend, and holiday hours.

Position Details

Full-Time
Schedule: Variable evenings, nights, weekends, and holidays
Potential shifts: 3:00 PM – 11:00 PM, 5:00 PM – 1:00 AM, or 11:00 PM – 7:00 AM
Emergency department and inpatient behavioral health consultation services
Acute and chronic psychiatric patient populations
Collaborative, multidisciplinary care environment

Position Qualifications

Nurse Practitioner (NP) Requirements
Graduation from an accredited Nurse Practitioner program
Master’s Degree or Doctorate in Nursing Practice
Current license to practice as a Nurse Practitioner in North Carolina
Current board certification as a Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner (PMHNP-BC) through a nationally recognized certifying body
Current prescriptive privileges and DEA license

Physician Assistant (PA) Requirements
Graduation from an accredited Physician Assistant program
Current license to practice as a Physician Assistant in North Carolina
Current certification through the National Commission on Certification of Physician Assistants (NCCPA)
Current or pending Certificate of Added Qualifications (CAQ) in Psychiatry preferred
Current prescriptive privileges and DEA license

Job Summary
The Behavioral Health Advanced Practice Provider provides specialized psychiatric evaluation, consultation, and treatment services to patients experiencing acute and chronic behavioral health conditions within Atrium Health’s emergency department and inpatient care settings.

The provider will assess, diagnose, and manage psychiatric conditions, respond to behavioral health consultation requests, and develop individualized treatment recommendations to support patient safety, stabilization, and appropriate disposition.

Working in collaboration with psychiatrists, emergency medicine providers, hospitalists, nursing staff, social workers, case managers, and other healthcare professionals, the APP will facilitate timely access to psychiatric services, promote effective care coordination, and support safe transitions across levels of care.

This position provides essential behavioral health coverage during evening, overnight, weekend, and holiday hours, contributing to improved patient access, continuity of care, and efficient clinical workflows.

When you join Atrium Health, you become part of an inclusive culture that values collaboration, innovation, and compassion. Practice where your voice is valued, your expertise in behavioral health is supported, and you have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact on patients navigating acute and complex psychiatric conditions.

Join our Behavioral Health team and help expand access to timely, compassionate, and comprehensive psychiatric care for the patients and communities we serve.

Make an impact throughout the surgical patient journey as an Advanced Practice Provider within the Department of Surgery.

This APP serves as a key clinical member of the surgical team, delivering high-quality, patient-centered care across the continuum of surgical services. With a strong focus on ambulatory specialty care, this role provides the opportunity to independently manage post-operative and surveillance patients while developing expertise in complex wound and ostomy care.

Working closely with surgeons and interdisciplinary teams, the APP plays an important role in coordinating care, supporting patients throughout their surgical journey, and helping optimize outcomes across care settings.

• Opportunity for autonomous outpatient patient management

We are seeking a highly motivated and collaborative Advanced Practice Provider (Physician Assistant or Nurse Practitioner) to join our growing Urogynecology and Pelvic Reconstructive Surgery team. This position provides a unique opportunity to deliver specialized, patient-centered care to women with pelvic floor disorders in an office based setting.

The APP will work closely with fellowship-trained urogynecologists to evaluate, diagnose, and manage conditions including urinary incontinence, pelvic organ prolapse, fecal incontinence, and other pelvic floor dysfunctions. This role will be focused on office-based urogynecology.

Location & Setting:

• Charlotte – office located on campus of Atrium Health Mercy Hospital
• Outpatient

Scope of Practice/What You’ll Do:

Clinical Care

• Perform comprehensive history and physical examinations with a focus on pelvic floor disorders.
• Diagnose and manage urinary incontinence (stress, urge, mixed), pelvic organ prolapse, overactive bladder, and bowel dysfunction
• Develop and implement individualized treatment plans, including conservative, medical, and surgical treatment options.
• Provide patient education on pelvic health, lifestyle modification, and surgical treatment options
• Perform office-based procedures such as:
• Pessary fitting and management
• PTNS (Percutaneous Tibial Nerve Stimulation)
• Bladder Catheterization
• Participate in perioperative care including pre-op evaluation and post-op follow-up

Team & Support Structure

• Team composed of 3 MDs, 7 APPs
• Collaborative model supporting a high volume surgical practice
• Onboarding/training support provided by numerous MDs, APPs and Chief APP as well as the Center for Advanced Practice

Why This Role / Differentiators

• Work on a close-knit team in a high-volume surgical practice
• Collaborate with physician fellows and residents
• Opportunity to teach students and residents
• Opportunity for growth in leadership

Qualifications

• Graduate of an accredited Physician Assistant or Nurse Practitioner program
• Current state licensure and board certification (PA-C or NP)
• DEA licensure (or eligibility)
• Minimum of 1–2 years of clinical experience preferred; women’s health, urology, gynecology, or surgical experience strongly desirable

Benefits/Supplemental Benefits:

• Paid Time Off programs available for eligible positions

The Advanced Practice Provider (APP) is credential by the medical staff and functions within their scope of practice in their jurisdictional area and in accordance with organizational medical staff bylaws. They are responsible for providing evidenced-based care for the management of patients, including assessment, implementation and evaluation of a detailed plan of care, which incorporates diagnostic and therapeutic interventions. The APP demonstrates competency in providing age-appropriate care to patients as defined by certification and training and provides family centered care to meet family needs, including psychological support, education and discharge planning in conjunction with other related disciplines.

The APP initiates, participates and collaborates with divisional and organizational multi-disciplinary staff to provide and support evidence-based education, quality improvement and research. They participate in professional and organizational activities that contribute to improving patient care, the scientific knowledge base of advanced practice, program operation, and individual professional development. The APP provides leadership within their respective clinical area through participation in division projects and mentorship of others. They contribute to department and organization wide initiatives, representing advanced practice and promoting the role of the advanced practice provider.

Minimum Education
Master's Degree Nurse Practitioner
Master's or Doctoral degree as a Nurse Practitioner from an accredited program and eligibility for medical staff credentialing required.

Physician Assistant

Clinical Nurse Specialist
Master’s or Doctorate degree in the clinical specialty area in which they practice from an accredited program and eligibility for medical staff credentialing required.
(Required)

Minimum of 0 years of experience as an Advanced Practice Provider (Required)

Strong knowledge of clinical specialty and services.
